title: Aviation mechanic maintenance and inspection records study guide
description: Study guide to 14 CFR Part 43 records: overhauled and rebuilt entries, 43.9 and 43.11 entries, life-limited parts and FAA Form 337 (Appendix B).
intro: 14 CFR 43.2, 43.9, 43.10, 43.11 and Appendix B to Part 43 set the FAA's rules for maintenance and inspection records. This guide sets out what the regulation text states on when an item may be described as overhauled or rebuilt, the maintenance record entry required after maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding or alteration, the control and transfer of life-limited parts, the entry required after inspections under parts 91, 125 and 135, the list of discrepancies and inoperative placards, and how major repairs and major alterations are recorded on FAA Form 337. goraedu does not train, test or certificate mechanics, and this is not an FAA test. Every point links to the regulation and quotes its exact words.

points.text: No person may describe an aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, appliance, or component part as being overhauled in any required maintenance entry or form unless both conditions in 43.2(a) are met.
points.quote: No person may describe in any required maintenance entry or form an aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, appliance, or component part as being overhauled unless

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.2, Records of overhaul and rebuilding (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: First condition: using methods, techniques, and practices acceptable to the Administrator, the item has been disassembled, cleaned, inspected, repaired as necessary, and reassembled.
points.quote: Using methods, techniques, and practices acceptable to the Administrator, it has been disassembled, cleaned, inspected, repaired as necessary, and reassembled; and

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.2, Records of overhaul and rebuilding (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Second condition: the item has been tested by one of two options: in accordance with approved standards and technical data, or in accordance with current standards and technical data acceptable to the Administrator that were developed and documented by the holder of the type certificate, supplemental type certificate, or a material, part, process, or appliance approval under part 21.
points.quote: It has been tested in accordance with approved standards and technical data, or in accordance with current standards and technical data acceptable to the Administrator, which have been developed and documented by the holder of the type certificate, supplemental type certificate, or a material, part, process, or appliance approval under part 21 of this chapter.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.2, Records of overhaul and rebuilding (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: No person may describe an item as being rebuilt in any required maintenance entry or form unless it has been disassembled, cleaned, inspected, repaired as necessary, reassembled, and tested to the same tolerances and limits as a new item.
points.quote: No person may describe in any required maintenance entry or form an aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, appliance, or component part as being rebuilt unless it has been disassembled, cleaned, inspected, repaired as necessary, reassembled, and tested to the same tolerances and limits as a new item

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.2, Records of overhaul and rebuilding (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: A rebuilt item uses either new parts or used parts; the used parts must conform either to new part tolerances and limits or to approved oversized or undersized dimensions.
points.quote: using either new parts or used parts that either conform to new part tolerances and limits or to approved oversized or undersized dimensions.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.2, Records of overhaul and rebuilding (as of Nov 4, 2026)

topics.name: Maintenance record entries

points.text: Except as provided in 43.9(b) and (c), each person who maintains, performs preventive maintenance, rebuilds, or alters an aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, appliance, or component part shall make an entry in the maintenance record of that equipment containing the information listed in 43.9(a).
points.quote: Except as provided in paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section, each person who maintains, performs preventive maintenance, rebuilds, or alters an aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, appliance, or component part shall make an entry in the maintenance record of that equipment containing the following information:

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.9, Content, form, and disposition of maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alteration records (except inspections performed in accordance with part 91, part 125, § 135.411(a)(1), and § 135.419 of this chapter) (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The entry contains a description of work performed, or a reference to data acceptable to the Administrator.
points.quote: A description (or reference to data acceptable to the Administrator) of work performed.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.9, Content, form, and disposition of maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alteration records (except inspections performed in accordance with part 91, part 125, § 135.411(a)(1), and § 135.419 of this chapter) (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The entry contains the date of completion of the work performed.
points.quote: The date of completion of the work performed.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.9, Content, form, and disposition of maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alteration records (except inspections performed in accordance with part 91, part 125, § 135.411(a)(1), and § 135.419 of this chapter) (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The entry contains the name of the person performing the work if that person is other than the person approving the work under 43.9(a)(4).
points.quote: The name of the person performing the work if other than the person specified in paragraph (a)(4) of this section.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.9, Content, form, and disposition of maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alteration records (except inspections performed in accordance with part 91, part 125, § 135.411(a)(1), and § 135.419 of this chapter) (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: If the work has been performed satisfactorily, the entry contains the signature, certificate number, and kind of certificate held by the person approving the work.
points.quote: If the work performed on the aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, appliance, or component part has been performed satisfactorily, the signature, certificate number, and kind of certificate held by the person approving the work.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.9, Content, form, and disposition of maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alteration records (except inspections performed in accordance with part 91, part 125, § 135.411(a)(1), and § 135.419 of this chapter) (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: That signature constitutes the approval for return to service only for the work performed.
points.quote: The signature constitutes the approval for return to service only for the work performed.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.9, Content, form, and disposition of maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alteration records (except inspections performed in accordance with part 91, part 125, § 135.411(a)(1), and § 135.419 of this chapter) (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Each holder of an air carrier operating certificate or an operating certificate issued under Part 121 or 135 that is required by its approved operations specifications to provide for a continuous airworthiness maintenance program shall make a record of the maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alteration on the equipment it operates in accordance with the applicable provisions of Part 121 or 135, as appropriate.
points.quote: Each holder of an air carrier operating certificate or an operating certificate issued under Part 121 or 135, that is required by its approved operations specifications to provide for a continuous airworthiness maintenance program, shall make a record of the maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alteration, on aircraft, airframes, aircraft engines, propellers, appliances, or component parts which it operates in accordance with the applicable provisions of Part 121 or 135 of this chapter, as appropriate.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.9, Content, form, and disposition of maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alteration records (except inspections performed in accordance with part 91, part 125, § 135.411(a)(1), and § 135.419 of this chapter) (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: 43.9 does not apply to persons performing inspections in accordance with Part 91, 125, § 135.411(a)(1), or § 135.419.
points.quote: This section does not apply to persons performing inspections in accordance with Part 91, 125, § 135.411(a)(1), or § 135.419 of this chapter.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.9, Content, form, and disposition of maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alteration records (except inspections performed in accordance with part 91, part 125, § 135.411(a)(1), and § 135.419 of this chapter) (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: In addition to the 43.9(a) entry, major repairs and major alterations shall be entered on a form, and the form disposed of, in the manner prescribed in appendix B, by the person performing the work.
points.quote: In addition to the entry required by paragraph (a) of this section, major repairs and major alterations shall be entered on a form, and the form disposed of, in the manner prescribed in appendix B, by the person performing the work.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.9, Content, form, and disposition of maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alteration records (except inspections performed in accordance with part 91, part 125, § 135.411(a)(1), and § 135.419 of this chapter) (as of Nov 4, 2026)

notCovered: Who may approve work for return to service, and the content of Parts 121 and 135 record rules, are outside the sections this guide covers.

topics.name: Life-limited parts

points.text: A life-limited part means any part for which a mandatory replacement limit is specified in the type design, the Instructions for Continued Airworthiness, or the maintenance manual.
points.quote: Life-limited part means any part for which a mandatory replacement limit is specified in the type design, the Instructions for Continued Airworthiness, or the maintenance manual.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.10, Disposition of life-limited aircraft parts (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Life status means the accumulated cycles, hours, or any other mandatory replacement limit of a life-limited part.
points.quote: Life status means the accumulated cycles, hours, or any other mandatory replacement limit of a life-limited part.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.10, Disposition of life-limited aircraft parts (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: When a life-limited part is temporarily removed and reinstalled for the purpose of performing maintenance, no disposition under 43.10(c) is required if all three conditions in 43.10(b) are met.
points.quote: When a life-limited part is temporarily removed and reinstalled for the purpose of performing maintenance, no disposition under paragraph (c) of this section is required if

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.10, Disposition of life-limited aircraft parts (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: First condition: the life status of the part has not changed.
points.quote: The life status of the part has not changed;

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.10, Disposition of life-limited aircraft parts (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Second condition: the removal and reinstallation is performed on the same serial numbered product.
points.quote: The removal and reinstallation is performed on the same serial numbered product; and

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.10, Disposition of life-limited aircraft parts (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Third condition: that product does not accumulate time in service while the part is removed.
points.quote: That product does not accumulate time in service while the part is removed.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.10, Disposition of life-limited aircraft parts (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Except as provided in 43.10(b), after April 15, 2002 each person who removes a life-limited part from a type-certificated product must ensure that the part is controlled using one of the methods in 43.10(c).
points.quote: Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, after April 15, 2002 each person who removes a life-limited part from a type-certificated product must ensure that the part is controlled using one of the methods in this paragraph.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.10, Disposition of life-limited aircraft parts (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The method must deter the installation of the part after it has reached its life limit.
points.quote: The method must deter the installation of the part after it has reached its life limit.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.10, Disposition of life-limited aircraft parts (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: One option is a record keeping system that substantiates the part number, serial number, and current life status of the part. The record must be updated with the current life status each time the part is removed from a type certificated product, and the system may include electronic, paper, or other means of record keeping.
points.quote: The part may be controlled using a record keeping system that substantiates the part number, serial number, and current life status of the part. Each time the part is removed from a type certificated product, the record must be updated with the current life status. This system may include electronic, paper, or other means of record keeping.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.10, Disposition of life-limited aircraft parts (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: One option is a tag or other record attached to the part, including the part number, serial number, and current life status. Each time the part is removed from a type certificated product, either a new tag or record must be created, or the existing one must be updated with the current life status.
points.quote: A tag or other record may be attached to the part. The tag or record must include the part number, serial number, and current life status of the part. Each time the part is removed from a type certificated product, either a new tag or record must be created, or the existing tag or record must be updated with the current life status.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.10, Disposition of life-limited aircraft parts (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: One option is legible non-permanent marking showing current life status, updated each time the part is removed from a type certificated product; if the mark is removed, another method in 43.10 may be used. The mark must be accomplished in accordance with the instructions under § 45.16 in order to maintain the integrity of the part.
points.quote: The part may be legibly marked using a non-permanent method showing its current life status. The life status must be updated each time the part is removed from a type certificated product, or if the mark is removed, another method in this section may be used. The mark must be accomplished in accordance with the instructions under § 45.16 of this chapter in order to maintain the integrity of the part.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.10, Disposition of life-limited aircraft parts (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: One option is legible permanent marking showing current life status, updated each time the part is removed from a type certificated product. Unless the part is permanently removed from use on type certificated products, the permanent mark must be accomplished in accordance with the instructions under § 45.16.
points.quote: The part may be legibly marked using a permanent method showing its current life status. The life status must be updated each time the part is removed from a type certificated product. Unless the part is permanently removed from use on type certificated products, this permanent mark must be accomplished in accordance with the instructions under § 45.16 of this chapter in order to maintain the integrity of the part.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.10, Disposition of life-limited aircraft parts (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: One option is segregation using methods that deter its installation on a type-certificated product. These methods must include, at least, maintaining a record of the part number, serial number, and current life status, and ensuring the part is physically stored separately from parts that are currently eligible for installation.
points.quote: The part may be segregated using methods that deter its installation on a type-certificated product. These methods must include, at least—(i) Maintaining a record of the part number, serial number, and current life status, and (ii) Ensuring the part is physically stored separately from parts that are currently eligible for installation.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.10, Disposition of life-limited aircraft parts (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: One option is mutilation to deter installation in a type certificated product. The mutilation must render the part beyond repair and incapable of being reworked to appear to be airworthy.
points.quote: The part may be mutilated to deter its installation in a type certificated product. The mutilation must render the part beyond repair and incapable of being reworked to appear to be airworthy.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.10, Disposition of life-limited aircraft parts (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Another option is any other method approved or accepted by the FAA.
points.quote: Other methods. Any other method approved or accepted by the FAA.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.10, Disposition of life-limited aircraft parts (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Each person who removes a life-limited part from a type certificated product and later sells or otherwise transfers it must transfer with the part the mark, tag, or other record used to comply with 43.10, unless the part is mutilated before it is sold or transferred.
points.quote: Each person who removes a life-limited part from a type certificated product and later sells or otherwise transfers that part must transfer with the part the mark, tag, or other record used to comply with this section, unless the part is mutilated before it is sold or transferred.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.10, Disposition of life-limited aircraft parts (as of Nov 4, 2026)

notCovered: The marking instructions in § 45.16 are named by 43.10 but are not set out here.

topics.name: Inspection record entries

points.text: After any inspection performed in accordance with part 91, 125, § 135.411(a)(1), or § 135.419, the person approving or disapproving the equipment for return to service shall make an entry in its maintenance record containing the information listed in 43.11(a).
points.quote: The person approving or disapproving for return to service an aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, appliance, or component part after any inspection performed in accordance with part 91, 125, § 135.411(a)(1), or § 135.419 shall make an entry in the maintenance record of that equipment containing the following information:

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.11, Content, form, and disposition of records for inspections conducted under parts 91 and 125 and §§ 135.411(a)(1) and 135.419 of this chapter (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The entry contains the type of inspection and a brief description of the extent of the inspection.
points.quote: The type of inspection and a brief description of the extent of the inspection.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.11, Content, form, and disposition of records for inspections conducted under parts 91 and 125 and §§ 135.411(a)(1) and 135.419 of this chapter (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The entry contains the date of the inspection and aircraft total time in service.
points.quote: The date of the inspection and aircraft total time in service.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.11, Content, form, and disposition of records for inspections conducted under parts 91 and 125 and §§ 135.411(a)(1) and 135.419 of this chapter (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The entry contains the signature, the certificate number, and kind of certificate held by the person approving or disapproving for return to service.
points.quote: The signature, the certificate number, and kind of certificate held by the person approving or disapproving for return to service the aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, appliance, component part, or portions thereof.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.11, Content, form, and disposition of records for inspections conducted under parts 91 and 125 and §§ 135.411(a)(1) and 135.419 of this chapter (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Except for progressive inspections, if the aircraft is found to be airworthy and approved for return to service, the entry contains the following or a similarly worded statement.
points.quote: Except for progressive inspections, if the aircraft is found to be airworthy and approved for return to service, the following or a similarly worded statement—“I certify that this aircraft has been inspected in accordance with (insert type) inspection and was determined to be in airworthy condition.”

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.11, Content, form, and disposition of records for inspections conducted under parts 91 and 125 and §§ 135.411(a)(1) and 135.419 of this chapter (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Except for progressive inspections, if the aircraft is not approved for return to service because of needed maintenance, noncompliance with applicable specifications, airworthiness directives, or other approved data, the entry contains the following or a similarly worded statement, which says a dated list of discrepancies and unairworthy items has been provided for the aircraft owner or operator.
points.quote: Except for progressive inspections, if the aircraft is not approved for return to service because of needed maintenance, noncompliance with applicable specifications, airworthiness directives, or other approved data, the following or a similarly worded statement—“I certify that this aircraft has been inspected in accordance with (insert type) inspection and a list of discrepancies and unairworthy items dated (date) has been provided for the aircraft owner or operator.”

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.11, Content, form, and disposition of records for inspections conducted under parts 91 and 125 and §§ 135.411(a)(1) and 135.419 of this chapter (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: For progressive inspections, the entry contains the following or a similarly worded statement, naming the routine and detailed inspections performed and whether the aircraft or components are approved or disapproved for return to service.
points.quote: For progressive inspections, the following or a similarly worded statement—“I certify that in accordance with a progressive inspection program, a routine inspection of (identify whether aircraft or components) and a detailed inspection of (identify components) were performed and the (aircraft or components) are (approved or disapproved) for return to service.”

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.11, Content, form, and disposition of records for inspections conducted under parts 91 and 125 and §§ 135.411(a)(1) and 135.419 of this chapter (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: If disapproved after a progressive inspection, the entry further states that a dated list of discrepancies and unairworthy items has been provided to the aircraft owner or operator.
points.quote: If disapproved, the entry will further state “and a list of discrepancies and unairworthy items dated (date) has been provided to the aircraft owner or operator.”

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.11, Content, form, and disposition of records for inspections conducted under parts 91 and 125 and §§ 135.411(a)(1) and 135.419 of this chapter (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: If an inspection is conducted under an inspection program provided for in part 91, 125, or § 135.411(a)(1), the entry must identify the inspection program and the part of it accomplished, and contain a statement that the inspection was performed in accordance with the inspections and procedures for that particular program.
points.quote: If an inspection is conducted under an inspection program provided for in part 91, 125, or § 135.411(a)(1), the entry must identify the inspection program, that part of the inspection program accomplished, and contain a statement that the inspection was performed in accordance with the inspections and procedures for that particular program.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.11, Content, form, and disposition of records for inspections conducted under parts 91 and 125 and §§ 135.411(a)(1) and 135.419 of this chapter (as of Nov 4, 2026)

notCovered: The inspections themselves (which ones are required and when) are set by other parts and are not described here.

topics.name: Discrepancy lists and placards

points.text: If the person performing any inspection required by part 91 or 125 or § 135.411(a)(1) finds that the aircraft is unairworthy or does not meet the applicable type certificate data, airworthiness directives, or other approved data upon which its airworthiness depends, that person must give the owner or lessee a signed and dated list of those discrepancies.
points.quote: If the person performing any inspection required by part 91 or 125 or § 135.411(a)(1) of this chapter finds that the aircraft is unairworthy or does not meet the applicable type certificate data, airworthiness directives, or other approved data upon which its airworthiness depends, that persons must give the owner or lessee a signed and dated list of those discrepancies.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.11, Content, form, and disposition of records for inspections conducted under parts 91 and 125 and §§ 135.411(a)(1) and 135.419 of this chapter (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: For items permitted to be inoperative under § 91.213(d)(2), that person shall place a placard that meets the aircraft's airworthiness certification regulations on each inoperative instrument and the cockpit control of each item of inoperative equipment, marking it "Inoperative."
points.quote: For those items permitted to be inoperative under § 91.213(d)(2) of this chapter, that person shall place a placard, that meets the aircraft's airworthiness certification regulations, on each inoperative instrument and the cockpit control of each item of inoperative equipment, marking it “Inoperative,”

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.11, Content, form, and disposition of records for inspections conducted under parts 91 and 125 and §§ 135.411(a)(1) and 135.419 of this chapter (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: That person shall also add those items to the signed and dated list of discrepancies given to the owner or lessee.
points.quote: and shall add the items to the signed and dated list of discrepancies given to the owner or lessee.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.11, Content, form, and disposition of records for inspections conducted under parts 91 and 125 and §§ 135.411(a)(1) and 135.419 of this chapter (as of Nov 4, 2026)

notCovered: Which items § 91.213(d)(2) permits to be inoperative is outside this guide.

topics.name: FAA Form 337 and Appendix B

points.text: Except as provided in Appendix B paragraphs (b), (c), and (d), each person performing a major repair or major alteration has three duties under Appendix B(a).
points.quote: Except as provided in paragraphs (b), (c), and (d) of this appendix, each person performing a major repair or major alteration shall

points.quote: Execute FAA Form 337 at least in duplicate; (2) Give a signed copy of that form to the aircraft owner; and

notCovered: The examples of major repairs and major alterations in Appendix A, and the fields of FAA Form 337 itself, are not covered here. §§ 43.7, 43.17 and 91.417 are named only where Appendix B names them.
